metadata.scope: Entire mutation architecture: control plane, orchestrator, backend adapter, mutmut, cache, workspace, evidence, result classification

verify_py_mutation_path.status: VERIFIED - this is the path that actually executes in CI

mutation_execution_orchestrator_path.status: PARTIALLY_VERIFIED - exists but NOT called by verify.py

duplicate_authorities.name: Mutation Orchestration
duplicate_authorities.risk: HIGH - Two parallel mutation execution paths exist. The verify.py path uses the simpler mutation_runner.py directly. The more sophisticated MutationOrchestrator (M9-C44) with parallel execution, sharding, and campaign management is NOT wired into the verify.py path. This means the M9-C44 features (parallel execution, sharding, workspace management) are not actually being used in production.

duplicate_authorities.name: Mutation Result Classification
duplicate_authorities.authority_a: MutationResult in mutation_contract.py (M9-C42.5) - buckets: killed, survived, no_tests, timeout, suspicious, not_checked
duplicate_authorities.authority_b: MutationResult in mutation_execution/domain_model.py (M9-C44.1) - states: KILLED, SURVIVED, EQUIVALENT, NO_TESTS, TIMEOUT, EXECUTION_ERROR, INVALID_MUTANT, NOT_EXECUTED, CANCELLED, UNKNOWN
duplicate_authorities.actual_used: Both - mutation_runner.py uses mutation_contract.py MutationResult; MutationOrchestrator uses domain_model.py MutationResult
duplicate_authorities.risk: MEDIUM - Two MutationResult dataclasses with different vocabularies. The mutation_runner.py path uses the contract one (6 buckets). The MutationOrchestrator uses the domain model one (10 states). The two are not directly compatible.

duplicate_authorities.name: Cache System
duplicate_authorities.authority_a: VerificationCache in cache.py - content-aware cache for verification runs
duplicate_authorities.authority_b: MutationCache in mutation_execution/cache.py - per-mutant result cache
duplicate_authorities.risk: LOW - Two separate cache systems for different concerns. The verification cache is for overall run results; the mutation cache is for per-mutant results. No overlap in scope.

mutation_population.scope_seam: transaction_intelligence and financial_intelligence were admitted in M9-C42.26 but the executable selection contract was only extended in M9-C43.0. The scope is NOT truly repository-wide - it covers 14 specific engines, not all backend/src/.

three_gate_classification.notes: Three-gate classification is properly implemented. On Gate A FAIL, Gate C is NOT evaluated and the returned verdict is 'NOT EVALUABLE'.

verification_cache.notes: R-CACHE-1 fix - any content change forces fresh run via tree_digest

mutation_cache.notes: Per-mutant cache keyed by configuration fingerprint

interruption_resume.mutation_runner_path: VERIFIED - signal handlers (SIGTERM, SIGINT) + atexit restore config. _MutationSafety context manager ensures restoration.
interruption_resume.mutation_orchestrator_path: VERIFIED - workspace persistence via create_workspace()/resume_workspace(). Campaign identity preserved.
interruption_resume.previous_claim: C45 claimed interruption/resume during active mutation execution. The actual evidence shows the interruption was BEFORE execution (baseline gate failure), not during active execution.

result_classification.ambiguous: VERIFIED - SUSPICIOUS bucket in mutation_contract.py, UNKNOWN state in domain_model.py
result_classification.automation: AUTOMATED via three-gate classification + InfrastructureFailureKind enum

conclusion.parallel_path: MutationOrchestrator in mutation_execution/ exists but is NOT wired into verify.py
conclusion.evidence: VERIFIED - mutation-summary.json + measurement-truth.json with full provenance
conclusion.risk: MEDIUM - The M9-C44 MutationOrchestrator with parallel/sharding capabilities exists but is not wired in. The verify.py path uses the simpler M9-C42.5 runner.
